column1: # Storage growth targets sampled by `disk-janitor --check` (growth-watch.py). Read-only.
# One row per target, tab-separated: label<TAB>path<TAB>owner[<TAB>alert GB]
# A path with a glob wildcard samples each matching directory as its own key, and the
# label is their total, so an alert names the one worktree or scratchpad that grew.
# `~` and {uid} are expanded. `docker:<type>` reads a `docker system df` row (Images,
# Containers, Local Volumes, Build Cache); `docker:volumes/<glob>` reads matching volumes
# from `docker system df -v`, which takes minutes on a busy daemon. The owner is printed
# on the alert: name whoever produces the growth, not the path.
# ~/.Trash is not listed: macOS privacy protection (TCC) denies it to a LaunchAgent without
# Full Disk Access, so the hourly check could only ever record `denied` for it.
